newsitem.title: UK: Nordics grab attention in crosses, gain on mark.
newsitem.headline: Nordics grab attention in crosses, gain on mark.

text.p: Nordic currencies gained on the mark by European midday as the focus turned to the recent robustness in Nordic securities markets amid a bare economic and political calendar today.

The Swedish and Norwegian crowns and the Finnish markka were also benefitting from the mark's weakness across the board today, following its fall to new multi-year lows against the dollar and British pound today and the yen overnight.
The Nordic currencies were trading around their highest levels against the mark in three to four months.
"Many people have recently felt that the Finnish markka has been undervalued, and to a lesser degree the Swedish crown as well," said one trader at a Scandinavian benk in London.
"But over the past week the focus has been on other things like the dollar and sterling, and there hadn't been much inflow into these (Nordic) currencies," he said.
The Norwegian crown was at 4.1715/40 per mark at 1050 GMT, near its session high and up from 4.1815/45 crowns in late European trade on Tuesday.
The Swedish crown was helped against the mark by some hefty sales of dollars and sterling for the crown yesterday and today, a trader at another Scandinavian bank said.
The Swedish crown was at its morning high of 4.3970/00 per mark against yesterday's 4.4175/05.
The attraction of the recently healthy Swedish securities market was also seen as a supportive factor.

"The latest data on foreign investors' buying of Swedish securities shows a significant increase, particularly in Swedish government bonds," said Richard Woodworth, European economist at Merrill Lynch.
He added that the moves in the crown were a result of trading to fund such heightened activity by foreign investors.

Traders said the story was a similar one for the Finnish markka, noting the bullishness in assets there with the Helsinki stock market rallying to a record high for the seventh straight session today.
"It doesn't seem to be speculative (markka) buying but investment buying. It's not that the currency is such good value, but the bond and equity markets are," the first bank trader said.
The markka was at 2.9655/85 per mark against 2.9700/30 in late Europe on Tuesday.
There was some scepticism about the Swedish crown gaining on a safe-haven status as a currency outside the European monetary union bloc in view of the uncertainties surrounding EMU.
In June, Sweden's ruling Social Democrats decided against joining EMU at its launch, although they kept the option of joining at a later date.
"That (Sweden's opt-out) had been the market consensus for at least a couple of months, and over the past weeks it hasn't been that much of a factor," Merrill's Woodworth said.
Meanwhile, the other European crosses were drifting amid a lack of fresh impetus.

Italian bonds continued their record-breaking rally, with the yield spread between key 10-year BTPs and bunds narrowing to its smallest-ever 93 basis points, but this failed to move the lira. Mark/lira was at 974.00/30 against Tuesday's 974.05/35.

French finance minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said the government planned 11.1 billion francs worth of new spending in 1997, adding that this would be financed by cuts in other areas and not by a net increase in this year's spending.
Mark/Paris was at 3.3732/37 against Tuesday's 3.3722/27.
-- Chizu Nomiyama, London Forex Desk, +44-171-542-
